utterances.text: Well, that is the way it should be. But, practically, not only my field of operation but also in other fields, I have to say we were very poorly organised. It was all at the embryonic stage, like the organisation of the army and everything else. The people worked so as to defend their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to cut you off too willingly, but do try and keep your answers short, if you can, because it saves time. Finally on this topic, at least for the moment, do you accept that in his promulgation of a plan for your department, Bozo Rajic made it clear that all documents and other factual evidence should be called on and taken over by the HZ HB institutions and stored for the administration of history -- sorry, stored by the administration of history -- that there was a policy, Mr. Prskalo, within your department for taking over and storing all records; correct? Nothing wrong with it, just is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, as for the storing, I remember this was a document with that request. However, I have to say that the wartime events and developments in the area in which I operated, that is, the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, prevented -- precluded any serious steps in that direction, because the events were succeeding one another so quickly that, at least from what I know, this was never -- this never came about. Besides, both in terms of territory and time, we were more or less isolated, and I already said that in my testimony today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it doesn't come as a surprise to you to see that two of the documents you signed ten years ago -- sorry, seven years ago -- should now be available from some archive somewhere for you to identify?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where these documents come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just deal with them very briefly, if we can, because I just want to move on. You were based where in January '93?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: January '93, I was in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: In the hotel in the centre of town practically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... office?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes, I had an office in which I also slept, because I had no other accommodation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have a secretary?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who typed your letters for you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I did not have a personal secretary, but we had a young woman who worked for the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: As they kept changing, I have to say I cannot recall the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sharing your office with anyone; for example, Valenta?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Oh, no. Mr. Valenta was a civilian. He was not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the initials "VS", who do they refer to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again just briefly so that we can move on, you were saying something, derived from one of these letters, about something that had happened to Mr. Kostroman. All sorts of dates were put to you and all sorts of summaries were actually put to you, but I would like you to tell us, please, what happened to Mr. Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I have not memorised all the details. A long time has gone by, some seven or eight years have gone by. But as far as I recollect, Mr. Kostroman, and I think this was on his way back from Kiseljak, was stopped by a group of Muslim soldiers, the so-called ABiH. They dragged him out of the car. And thanks to the unexpected arrival of the UNPROFOR vehicles, they saw that there was something going on, and they came over and found him there with the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not a question of the man having been taken away and detained anywhere else or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot tell exactly, with certainty, whether he was taken away from the highway, the Kiseljak-Busovaca road, but in any event he was made to step out of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he was rescued by the passing international UNPROFOR vehicle; you're sure about that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes, that is information that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he simply stopped by a group of Muslim soldiers, Mr. Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I heard, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, they were in a car themselves, were they, or on foot? You help us, please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: You mean the members of ABiH?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: That, I wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there's no question of Mr. Kostroman or anybody else being disarmed, simply being stopped and their weapons being taken from them or anything like that, is there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I believe that Mr. Kostroman did not have any weapons. He was a civilian. He was not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he travelling with?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: In addition to the driver, I don't know who else was there. My assumption is that no other person was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of there being anything like a couple of cars, because this was just a single car, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if you would be good enough now just to take the originals -- we can all look at them -- of these two exhibits that have been handed in. I would just like your help with them in a minute. 206 and 207, please. Let's look at 207 first. We can even perhaps put an original version on the ELMO. That's helpful, thank you. No, on this occasion can you put the B/C/S version or a B/C/S version on the ELMO so that the point can be seen. This is your signature, isn't it, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're telling us, as I understand it from the way you've produced this exhibit, that although of course it's a photocopy, this is an original document -- it's a copy of exactly what you prepared in January of 1993 at 9.10 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the bottom, we can see, five lines up from the bottom, "MP/VS". Well, now, you'll have to confirm this, but does that relate to you and to the person who has typed this document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what else would the other initials be but the typist's, please? You remember I asked you if you knew who "VS" was, and you didn't, but then you told us that the typists changed. So maybe it's an itinerant typist. What does the "VS" stand for if it doesn't stand for the typist?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe these were initials of the person who had typed this up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, shall we now look at the next document, please, 206/1. Look at them side by side, please. You see, if you look at the foot of this document, there's just the first little point to notice, in that it's not "VS" but the initials are now "SV", which sometimes happens in your country, doesn't it? Sometimes people put one name first and their family name second, and sometimes they do it the other way around, so there's nothing surprising in that, is there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's -- I'm so sorry. But it's likely to be the typist, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. It could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's only three days away from the other document, and it's perfectly obvious, if we look at the two documents side by side, that they've been prepared in a different style in several ways; for example, whether you indent a paragraph, whether you have a line between a paragraph, whether in the date you use the "O" from the alphabet for "01" for the month or whether you use the capital "O". There are various -- numerous stylistic differences. Let's have a look at the English version of this document. You follow it in the original. This is the document where you say you already know about the Muslim attack on the general secretary of HDZ, Ignac Kostroman, who has been saved by pure chance, that of course being a reference to the intervention of UNPROFOR; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this, please, Mr. Prskalo: An event of the seriousness of the type that you've referred of Mr. Kostroman being waylaid by some Muslims, would that have been recorded in detail somewhere in your office?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: It doesn't mean that it would have been recorded in detail. All information I sent out I practically wrote on the basis of information that I had received from someone. If such information was not detailed, I could not then pass on detailed information on to the next level of communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that, you already knew about the Muslim attack, it sounds as though there may have been some earlier information, some earlier recording of what had happened to Mr. Kostroman. There must have been records in your office, mustn't there, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this letter is the only document, is it, that exists to show that he was attacked and saved in the way you described?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: This is the document that I drafted, and whether someone else has a different kind of document, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to end this little topic, the signature, I know it's only a photocopy -- of course, no complaint about that -- but that is your signature, is it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that this document was prepared in 1993, or is there any chance that that document may have been prepared more recently?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Who would have done it? This is a document which I drafted at exactly that time. I remember this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I remember that this took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked about Mr. Kordic, your own opinion was that he became vice-president of the Republic, until you were corrected as to whether such a role existed. But it was your evidence that he was vice-president of the Republic. Why did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I made a mistake, by accident. He was vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or is the position that he was, for all practical purposes, the deputy to the man Boban, and therefore effectively the vice-president?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: So far as I know, Mr. Kordic was never deputy to Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else in your area of the seniority, in political terms, that Mr. Kordic had?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know. You may have in mind, in the area where I was, there was also Muslim authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the HZ HB, in the HVO, however you like to look at it, in the Croatian side of your community at that time, please, was there any politician senior to Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: If you have in mind the area of Central Bosnia Operative Zone, the rank of Mr. Kordic there was the highest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anybody junior to Mr. Boban, in political terms -- that is, subordinate to Mr. Boban -- who was exercising political power in your area, other than Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prskalo, you were the gatherer of intelligence and information. You have told us that you were an enthusiastic politician for years. Now, was there any politician who lay between, in levels of authority, Kordic and Boban?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Let me just tell you that, in practical terms, when I went -- when I joined the HVO, I ceased to be a politician, and please bear this in mind when we talk about this. Because when I joined the HVO, I, in practical terms, assumed military duties. I had no insight, no contacts, in any events, and relations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two things arising from that. First, it's been said that military men weren't allowed to be engaged in politics. Where do you say that order can be found, just so that we can identify it and satisfy ourselves that such a restriction existed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I never had on me any document relating to this, but when the IPD was organised, we pointed this out. You need to know that in all fields, we were in the initial stages of organisation, and that we cannot say, in any field, including the IPD, about a regular establishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand your answer, but I will move on with this question: Are you saying that you simply decided yourself you shouldn't be involved in politics? Is that what you're saying? Or was there some external rule that restricted your involvement in politics?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, that could not have been my own decision. This was valid in all areas of IPD activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second point arising from your answer is this: Even if there were any agreement or restriction on active involvement in politics, can you please explain to us how you were shielded for this period of time, long period of time, shielded from any information showing who were the politicians working in your area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I did not fully understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that because in some way you were a soldier, you couldn't help the Judges, to whom this answer is going to be directed, you couldn't help them with whether there was a politician between Kordic and Boban. What is it that kept such information, such reality, from your eyes and ears, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I am saying to you that I did not have the information, who it was, whether there was someone. You must know that the wartime events were such, and my preoccupation was with the work with which I was tasked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reality, Mr. Prskalo, is you know perfectly well that Mr. Kordic was the senior politician in the area, senior to everyone except Boban, and you're not prepared to tell the Judges that. Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: This is not a secret, and I don't think that it is a secret even to this Trial Chamber, that Mr. Boban was number-one man of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That wasn't the point. The point was: Was there any politician between Mr. Boban and Mr. Kordic? Now, can you help us on that, or not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I believe that I was clear that I don't know whether there was anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you turned up at meetings where there were military and political representations on a regular basis, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that I was present at the meetings to which you are referring. But perhaps you're referring to press conferences. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Press conferences. You turned up at press conferences with politicians, with military men, who talked to the public and to the press. On one occasion, as we've seen -- the Judges have already seen the tape -- you starting off the conference with a prepared statement. And you're telling us that you have no idea of where the political power rested in Central Bosnia. Is that really your evidence, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I must tell you that the political -- for the political power in Central Bosnia, everybody had some of it. Wherever there were Croats, Croats had the power. Wherever there were Muslims, Muslims had the power. For instance, in Stari Vitez the majority was Muslims, so the power was Muslims, and you know what the distance was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not an answer to my question, but I'm going to move to another question. Propaganda involves sometimes the truth, sometimes presentation of the truth, in particular ways, and sometimes it involves misinformation and lies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes, that is the characteristic of propaganda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us some examples, please, of lies advanced in the propaganda of the Croats in the time when you were working for the propaganda department?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I must tell you that I did not have such propaganda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So that your propaganda department traded in and used only the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this, for example, Mr. Blaskic's policy, that only the truth should be told?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: So far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were never aware of his changing that policy, even after the time when you were, very unfortunately, wounded and in hospital?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that from your experience of the man and the people working for him, if he threatened, for example, to blow something up, that wouldn't be misinformation or a lie; that would be a truth. He would really seriously intend to blow something up. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that he threatened to blow something up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know the man, you see, and you know his policy. If he said, "I'm going to blow this bridge up," for example, it wouldn't be an idle threat or anything of that sort; it would be for real, wouldn't it, because he didn't engage in false propaganda?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not engage in propaganda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Part of propaganda, as you have accepted, is presenting the truth, as you would say, in particular ways. And so for the propagandist, image is important. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know what you're trying to say with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally, a propagandist's work includes presenting information in the way that's going to be most effective, and sometimes the image -- I'll deal with the first point first. The propagandist's work includes presenting information in the way that's going to be most effective; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: If you're referring to the information that we were processing, I believe that I was clear in that our information, for the most part, was based on truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may come back to the words "for the most part" in a minute, but I'll progress with what I was starting to deal with. There was no need, was there, in Central Bosnia, to understate Mr. Blaskic's importance?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I'd say that there was no need either to understate or overstate his importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because he, so far as you know, was running the war, subject only to military orders that he may have received from somewhere else. Is that your position, please, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot speak about any orders, but if you are referring to the war, the Croats, or rather the HVO in the area in which it operated, was on the defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was running the military side of things, and to that extent he was running the war. That's, as I understand it, what you're telling us.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I'd say that it will be better to say that the circumstances required it. These were conflicts where people were defending themselves and defending their homesteads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Then I'd like you to help us with this, please: Why at all the press conferences is Kordic always sitting in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I couldn't really say why he used to sit like that. I don't know that anybody made any particular plan posed for sitting, and I'm not really sure. You are saying that. I'm not sure that he always sat in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... there's no middle, and so you're on the corner, and there's the three of them, with Kordic in the middle. But you were at these press conferences, you see. Tell the Judges: What looks to be -- who looks to be the man in charge, if you have a table with three people and one sits in the middle of it? Who looks to be in charge? The man in the middle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Not necessarily. The one in the middle need not be the principal, the central figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. If you think of any other answer you'd like to give to that question as the morning goes on, let me know. I'm going to try and deal very quickly with some chronological matters concerning yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And I'm going to cut out, Your Honour, most of the material that I had sketched in as topics I might cover, just so that we can try and deal with things quickly. But it will take me a few moments to read my notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a committed politician, and we know that from an early stage there was a split between Kljujic and the rest. What was your position on Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object, as I did yesterday. This was not mentioned in direct examination, not in a single word. I never mentioned Mr. Kljujic, nor did I touch upon those matters at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... Yes. Whose side are you on? That's the question, Mr. Prskalo. Perhaps you would tell us.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: If that is what you are asking me, to be quite honest, I was on nobody's side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not appreciate that there was a difference between what might be called the strong, or even the hard-line Croat view, and the view of Kljujic, for a mixed community? Are you telling us you didn't appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we go any further, while the witness is considering it, the transcript has left out my ruling, which was that the question went to credibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not appreciate the nature of the divide between Kljujic and Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I have to say that I simply did not know about any divide between Mr. Kljujic and Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I must intervene. This was not a proper question. Mr. Kljujic was the one who put Mr. Kordic in the place that he wanted. And the witness Kljujic never spoke about any rift between Mr. Kordic and Mr. Kljujic. So will the Prosecutor please refrain from that. At the time when Mr. Kljujic was the president of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Kordic was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I seem to remember some memoranda going between the two of them which showed a division. But I don't think we need take up any more time on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March 1992, where were you living? In Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: In March 1992 I was living in the town of Bugojno and worked for a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were already an active member of the party?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: At that time I was indeed a member of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But I held no office. I was only a deputy, a member of the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you not possibly become the president of the local party in September of 1990? I don't want to take long on this, but just think back.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I said in my statement today, and I can repeat it once again: I was elected the president of the Croat Democratic Union for Bugojno in 1992, and for about a year I was the president of that branch. And in 1991 I stopped to head the HDZ in Bugojno. I already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that the meeting where Kljujic was ousted, held in Bugojno on the 15th of March of 1992, you're not listed as being present, but as a matter of fact were you aware of the meeting? Just "yes" or "no".

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I do not know what you mean by was I aware. You mean did I have any information or was I aware? That is not one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the meeting and were you aware that Kljujic was ousted?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I learned about that from the press.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never publicly or in writing backed, for example, the Kljujic cause, did you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I believe I was clear enough today when I said that I was on nobody's side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. Just a matter of factual detail. We've heard from a witness describing circumstances in Gornji Vakuf at about the same time, June of 1992, Witness Damon. Would his account be accurate for circumstances in Gornji Vakuf in June 1992 when he says that he was arrested by the Territorial Defence, but they were obliged to take him to and he was dealt with by the HVO because they were effectively in control at that stage? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know about that event, and I don't know why you're asking me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you go to Gornji Vakuf regularly enough in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, in 1992, I didn't go to Gornji Vakuf all that often, even though that is the municipality where I was born, because you must know that the war had already begun, and while I was in Bugojno, sitting in my office, the Serb aggressor, the so-called Yugoslavia People's Army, was dropping bombs over Kupres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The HVO that you joined in your area, which is not so far from Gornji Vakuf, was it an organisation that as at that time already really superior to, for example, the Territorial Defence? Did it have effective power over the Territorial Defence right from June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say that the HVO was more powerful. From what I know about, the authority and the military forces were split up evenly. At the same time, we were talking about an alliance, because it was necessary to conduct all the operations jointly against the Chetniks, that is, the aggressors, because that was our purpose and that was in our interest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said something about, I think in your statement, about the role of the HVO, and possibly in your evidence. To whom was the HVO accountable in your overall organisations, please?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the HVO was, in part, a military organisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I think it was the military organisation, and your question seems to imply that the HVO was a political organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of the HVO? To whom did the HVO have to answer up the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: As for the chain of command, I don't know in detail how it was organised, because on the ground there were the troops, the armies of the armed people, and one can really comfortably say that it was a self-organisation for the defence of one's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you not aware of that which is contained in the Narodni list for September 1992, that the HVO and the HZ HB and every HVO member were accountable to the Presidency of the HZ HB; weren't you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I did not read that paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it was supposed to be widely distributed. You see, in paragraph 11 of your summary which you've signed, you said this, and by all means look at the B/C/S version of it -- it's in your pocket -- if you want to. You said you knew that Mate Boban held the position of the president of the Presidency, and he was president of the HZ HB and supreme commander of the armed forces of the HVO. What your statement doesn't say, and I would just like to know why, is that in fact the HVO was accountable to the Presidency. Now, that paragraph of your statement, Mr. Prskalo, was that your own terminology or had somebody helped you write that? Paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: This is my statement, and I know that Mr. Boban was the president of the HZ HB and also that he was the commander of the armed forces. I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Exhibit 223, please. Now, this is a document that I think shouldn't be totally unfamiliar to you. It's the 22nd of September, minutes of a meeting in Busovaca the 22nd of September, '92. So at that time, you were able to and did travel to Busovaca? You're shown as attending, you see. Yes. Do you remember the meeting? Mr. Prskalo, do you remember the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't recall that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back, you --

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: [Inaudible] record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. Let's work it out logically. This is a meeting of the Croat Defence Councils in the municipalities of Central Bosnia. There should have been a representative of your municipality; correct? Please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Just a moment. I really can't really remember that meeting. I don't know where it was held exactly. But it's possible that the mayor, the municipal mayor, was also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your name, you see, with your correct title, deputy commander of the Central Bosnia Defence Forces for Information and Propaganda, is listed. Two or three lines up from the bottom, you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: But I can't remember what the subject of the meeting was. All sorts of meetings were held at the time, and it is quite possible that one of those meetings were attended by both military and political representatives of the Croat people. I really can't remember the topic of the meeting. What was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I can help your memory. If you'll go on, please, to the heading "Travnik" -- and the Chamber can find it in the English version at the serial number at the bottom 377 and 378 -- but if you would just go on in the document, Mr. Prskalo, until you find the heading "Travnik", please. Probably page 4, I think, for you at the top. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: No, I didn't find "Travnik". I don't see where that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on page 4 at the top, and it's about halfway down.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Excuse me. This copy is very bad. I can't find "Travnik".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, Mr. Nice, you would just read out the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, before I come to the passage, it's this: Travnik was a Muslim-majority area; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, perhaps at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The decision was made at this meeting, and this is at the top of our page 378 in English, that: "The HVO government ..." and I'll read slowly, "... has recently been detaching itself from the joint municipal government. It has been planning the Central Bosnia chief HVO command to move to Travnik. Certain outpost-administered departments for Central Bosnia would be moved from Mostar to Travnik. The following are also moving to Travnik: Vice-president of the HZ HB, Valenta, the vice-president Dario Kordic, and then Kostroman." You appear to have been at the meeting, Mr. Prskalo. What would be the likely effect, do you think, of moving a Croat-based organisation, like the HVO was, lock, stock and barrel to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: If that happened, I don't know what the consequences might be. I can't answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Provocative, wouldn't it be?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately I must say that even before this meeting, if that is how it was, there had been provocations even before that, I mean from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not an answer to the question. Please. For a Croat-based -- effectively, a mono-Croat organisation to move to Travnik would have been an act of provocation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that is how the Muslim side might see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certainly didn't stand out in any way against such a decision, and you were there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I didn't even take part in the vote, in the voting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next paragraph, one after Kresevo, we come to -- sorry. The next paragraph at about 3 or 4, we come to Kresevo, and then we come to observations noted in all the municipalities, where it says that: "Muslims are behaving as if they ..." I'm so sorry. "... as if they had an exclusive right to power and as if they are the only fighters for B and H. All permits must be urgently made uniform and instructions used to jurisdiction. There has to be strong HVO propaganda everywhere." Well, you must have registered that and you must have acted in pursuance of it, as the propaganda officer; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I can say that I did not conduct any propaganda in this regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see, if we just go on one page in our English version -- I'm doing this for speed because the Court has seen this document before, but if we go on to about halfway down this general paragraph, there's this observation: "There is no Bosnian language, and it is an insult to the Croatians when anyone tries to make the Croatian language into some kind of a Bosnian language." Now, you may want to find that sentence to satisfy yourself. It's in the minutes. Would that be a view with which you agreed, please, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I have to say that I think that any member of any people in Europe would feel offended if anybody tried to change the name of his language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can see from this document that -- look right to the end of the document. "HVO military bodies for Central Bosnia shall prepare defence plans against possible attack by Islamic fundamentalist Mujahedin forces and introduce military discipline and uniform." Those were conclusions that you, amongst others, were happy with, Mr. Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: If you want me to say do you think that any side in Bosnia-Herzegovina failed to prepare defence, so we were preparing our defence. We had to defend ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Reverting back to your answer about changing the name of the language, what offence, if any, would the inhabitants of an area take if somebody changed its name effectively to something like "HZ HB"? What affect would that have on Muslim inhabitants? Would that offend them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but I suppose in the areas where the Muslims were the majority, quite possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will attempt to reduce what is outstanding to the bare bones this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We're going to adjourn now. Mr. Prskalo, would you remember, in this adjournment and any others, not to speak to anybody about your evidence and not to let anybody speak to you about it until it's over, and that includes the members of the Defence team. Thank you. If you would be back, please, at half past 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.02 p.m. 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 233, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prskalo, we've got a number of documents to look at. All of them, I hope, bar about one, very quickly. This document is coming to you. You'll be able to confirm that, in fact, your position was raised in October 1992, so that you became part of the working presidency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I did not understand. What working presidency?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'll explain it to me. This is a document that you can see, dated the 6th of October, from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Busovaca headquarters, stamped with the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna at Mostar. It's an extract from minutes of the meeting of the leaders of the Croatian Defence Council for Central Bosnia. Your name is listed as present. The meeting was in Busovaca. And the working presidency is said to be Valenta, Kostroman, and yourself. So of what were you a member of the working presidency?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Excuse me. I still don't see where my name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry about the quality of the photocopy, but if you look a third of the way down the first page where my finger is, if you look at the document, you can see, to the right of Kostroman, Marko Prskalo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I need to get -- we don't know about this number. There is already a document Z233, which is dated 6/10/92, and we have another one which is dated 22 September 1992. So can we please have that straightened out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go on. The registry can do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found your name, now, Mr. Prskalo? Well, I'm going to make a single point and then I'm going to move on, and counsel for Mr. Kordic can check the document. The meeting was not quorate; there weren't enough of you there to make decisions. But you must have been a party to the recommendations that were made. And one of those recommendations -- the Chamber can see it at 15 -- was a recommendation to resolve the issue of funding HZ HB bodies to be transferred to Travnik, so that you were indeed a party to the general plan to move HZ HB bodies to Travnik, which I think you would accept would be provocative.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Here, I found my name, but I have to say that I was never a member of any working presidency in any meetings. I was probably invited as a member of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you in due course whether in fact your role as a member of the propaganda department didn't place you very close to the general secret service and intelligence functions and whether, overall, you didn't perform some functions, to some degree, in the area, possibly for Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the witness now have the next Exhibit, please, which relates to the meeting on the 25th of October, 1992, at Sarajevo. That is an additional document. It's 255.2. We needn't look at the earlier documents, but for the purposes of the record, one of them is 248.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm told that 233 is, in fact, the same document as has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As the document I've just produced. All right. I'm sorry. 255.2, can it stay with the witness? Can I produce 252 first? My mistake. 252 coming. It's coming from the registry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 252, Mr. Prskalo, is some notes, typed notes, of the meeting at Sarajevo, and it may be indeed that you prepared these notes. Did you prepare notes of the meeting at Sarajevo that you attended?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I did not prepare these minutes, but I can confirm that I was in Sarajevo in October, when the negotiations were held at the airport, and I think that this was the first meeting of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second English sheet -- and it is in your version, Mr. Prskalo, I think on the second sheet as well -- it records that Colonel Blaskic stated that the HVO could not accept cessation of military activities unless Refik Lendo was handed over, and that Siber replied, "There has never been a war in which an army has handed over one of its commanders for trial," and said he could replace Lendo. Is the position that by that effort at negotiation, Blaskic showed himself to be unsuited for the tasks at Sarajevo, Mr. Prskalo, and is that the reason he was replaced?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, and besides, I'm not sure whether this is the authentic record and the correct information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that you had already was for the 25th of October, and we might as well just deal with that while it's there. That's Exhibit 255.2. That shows you being appointed, as representative of the commander of the Central Operative Zone, to a mixed commission which would be based in Novi Travnik. One way or another, you worked on many commissions covering the whole of the area, didn't you? Well, not the whole of the area, but a large part of the area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot say that it was a large area. In this case, when I talked today in my presentation, I said, and I can confirm to you this now, that I was a member of this mixed commission, because in this commission, in addition to the Croatian representatives, there were also representatives of the Muslim side. And the goal again was to calm down the situation in Novi Travnik, to re-establish peace, to exchange prisoners, and to work out the details on the materiel and other equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. 249, please. You're saying, of course, that Mr. Kordic had no military authority of any kind; is that correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't imagine him ever giving a military order, can you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot imagine it, and I don't think that Mr. Kordic ever issued any military orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bugojno was still your home area, was it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. During which period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This period in which we are now dealing, October '92.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: In October of '92, I was in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, look at the document, please. This is a document over the typed name of Kordic and Blaskic, you see that, with a handwritten note on the side about its receipt on the 24th of October, and it says: "We received reliable information that a unit of the BH army corresponding to two battalions is moving from Bugojno up the Bistrica River in the direction of Ravno, with the intention of joining up with Lendo's Muslim forces." Does that seem about right, in your recollection of events?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot recall, so I cannot confirm it. From this, I cannot even conclude what this is and whether this document is authentic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Should these units participate in the fighting, we shall use long-range artillery on Bugojno. Deadline: One hour after receipt of this message." You would have had an interest, at the very least, with what was happening in Bugojno. You say you had no knowledge of this as a plan and intention of Mr. Kordic and Mr. Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I don't know of such plans, and I don't believe that they existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 316.1, please. If you could show it, please, to the witness. This is the 15th of December of 1992, a press conference and a summary of it. The Chamber can see at the second sheet, starting at subparagraph 2, at this press conference Mr. Kordic took over. I'll read slowly. Perhaps the English version could be placed on the ELMO for the interpreters, if they don't have it, and I'll just read it out so far as necessary. "Mr. Kordic took over, focusing on two issues; problems in connection with the BH army and HVO cooperation. Previous suspicions and warnings of 5th Column activity within the ranks of the BH army prove to be right. An incident took place in Kaonik, where a high-ranking BH army commander defected to the Serbian side." It deals with the arrest of Muslim leaders and the possibility of friction between Croats and Muslims in Novi Travnik, dealing with the occupation of army buildings, and then goes on to deal with a mixed military working group. Would that be a typical press conference of Mr. Kordic's, to deal with such matters?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I believe that it is not, and I don't know that I was at such a conference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because he's dealing with military matters, isn't he, and that's what he regularly did?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you say that the matters I've just read out, problems in connection with the army, 5th Column activity, arrests of soldiers, they are not military matters; is that what you're telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: In a way, one could say so, but it is not an issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's not an issue. I thought you had said that Mr. Kordic was solely political and had nothing to do with the military, and I would like your help, please, as a person who knows about the press conferences, with how it comes that Mr. Kordic is dealing with military matters, please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I do not exclude the possibility that Mr. Kordic sometimes also addressed military issues, but he was not the person who decided or who led military matters. He was a political figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why, at these press conferences where there was soldiers present, didn't they deal with all the military matters? Please help us.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: In any event, the soldiers dealt with the military matters, and given the situation, I don't exclude the possibility that some civilians also addressed certain military issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of January of 1993, you were appointed to the personnel committee under Blaskic, no longer with Sliskovic. I don't need the exhibit if you'll accept that. It's Exhibit 359. Do you remember that you were appointed to the personnel committee?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot recall, but I would like to see the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 359, please. You see, on this day you were appointed to the personnel committee, along with Blaskic, Josic, Nakic and Sliskovic, and a very important committee it was, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Of course the personnel committee should be important, but I don't recall having taken any personnel decisions further to this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Very well. Well, we'll move on, for wont of time. There's a video to be played, or part of it. But before we come to that video, just tell me what it is you're saying about Busovaca and the attack. Are you saying Busovaca was the subject of an attack in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that this was an unprompted attack by Muslim forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which the Croats and HVO did not respond in any way?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I suppose they defended themselves, but they didn't do anything else?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Isn't it natural in any community, if you were attacked, that you should defend yourself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, what's the date of this attack by the Muslims on Busovaca, please?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: This was at the end of the month. I cannot recall now, but it was at the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was the very first violence, was it, in Busovaca, the attack by the Muslims; is that your account?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: There were incidents before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Let's just have a look at the video, please, if we may. It's 1705.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just give them another chance. Any chance that it's working?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to explain how you would -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's enough, to save time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that look familiar to you, please, Mr. Prskalo? This was the area of your operation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I see some damage here to some houses and some streets, but I cannot make out what place this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The evidence is that this is Busovaca and it's all the Muslim premises and the businesses. You were there. You were in charge of propaganda, receiving information and disseminating it. How did you deal, please, with the damage to Muslim businesses in Busovaca in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I must say that I did not handle even the houses which were damaged in the Croatian area. And I didn't recognise whether this is an authentic videotape from Busovaca, and from what period this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may say that, but take it, please, from me, and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, that the video has been played as a tape of Busovaca, and the evidence of the damage to Muslim premises has not been challenged. So it may be that that's accepted as having happened. Now, how come it's just Muslim premises that are damaged in Busovaca in January, if what you're saying is true, please?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: If these are really pictures of damaged Muslim business premises in Busovaca, I do not want to contradict. But I also need to tell the Trial Chamber that we had damages on the Busovaca side as well. We were in a very complex situation. There were individual incidents. I know very well that it happened, for instance, that Croatian premises were also mined in other places as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prskalo, you just saw this film. Could you recognise Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I have just said that I could not really recognise it. I couldn't say whether it was Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How long were you in Busovaca? Did you know the town?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really know Busovaca, but I did go there now and then. In my evidence at the beginning today, I said that being a member of the monitoring mission, I spent something over a month in Busovaca. But at that time I was not in the town itself. We were staying in the hotel in Busovaca, and the monitoring mission, or rather our teams, went out into the field to different areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you did not recognise it. It was a small town and you spent all the time there and you could not recognise the town from these images? Think about it, because it is the matter of credibility concerning you that arises. We can show you the film once again.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I do not know if it would make any difference. I said I could not recognise it. I just said that these are some streets in Bosnia. They are typical Bosnian houses. But whether that is indeed Busovaca or not, I cannot confirm that. I would be very happy to confirm that, because I do not want to deny it, if that is true. But I must tell the truth, and the truth is that I really cannot recognise, cannot say, whether these images come from Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've now said there were incidents on both sides. Don't let me lead you to say something you don't want to say and that isn't your evidence, but has it not been your account that there was, as it were, peace until the Muslims attacked Busovaca and its environs?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: No, I did not say that. Regrettably, there were incidents on different sides and in different areas. But when it comes to the facilities that I refer to, I believe I said, but I can repeat it also: It also happened -- it happened -- there were cases when Croats mined some facilities. There were people who, out of sheer envy, wanted to remove somebody. There was a very uncomfortable situation in the beginning. There was -- chaos set in. There was no authority, there was no state. Nothing was in working order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just hear it from you, then. Was there an unjustified HVO attack on Merdani, for example? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, before I move to the next exhibit, Mr. Prskalo, tell me this: In middle/late January of 1993, were you, and therefore others close to you, preoccupied by the fact that you had suffered unnecessary attacks from the Muslims, or were you in the middle of fighting which was equal on each side? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: All I can say is that I was worried by any attack, regardless of who had launched it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prskalo, you must know, broadly, whether in January 1993 you were the victims of wholly unjustified violence and warfare or whether you were engaged in fighting that was broadly equal on each side. Now, you must know. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: What I know is that we were attacked, and logically, in view of that, we were defending ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Blaskic was locked away in Kiseljak, wasn't he? He couldn't get back.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Colonel Blaskic could not return from Kiseljak because the Muslim forces had blocked all the roads and all the accesses to Busovaca and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you deal with in his absence? Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I must repeat here that at that time I did not have any contact with Mr. Kordic, because Kordic was a political figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which case, who did you deal with in Busovaca or Vitez? Who did you deal with?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? What period of time do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Blaskic was in Kiseljak, who did you deal with? Who was your immediate superior? To whom did you answer?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: We had the head of the staff. At that time I did not answer to anybody else, practically. I simply performed my duties regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the witness have, please, and may the Court have 2801.3, the transcript of the audiotape. 2801.2B. My mistake. Have you got 2801.2B? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is -- you have to -- Mr. Prskalo, there is an audiotape. It is admitted. Do you understand me? It's accepted that the voices on the tape are Kordic and Blaskic. It's suggested that the tape is the 24th of January, when Kordic was in Busovaca and when Blaskic was in Kiseljak. Do you understand me? There may or may not be issues as to whether somebody's cut the tape and completely made it up, but it's accepted that the voices are as they are shown to be. And I just want you to look at one passage of a conversation, which we'll come to, I hope, in the original version so that you'll be able to satisfy yourself that, as I read it to you, what's being said is correct. It's my mistake. Ms. Verhaag's got it all set up and I've mucked it up. Sorry. The original is 2801.2 A, apparently, the original transcript, and the translation is 2801.2B. And if you -- you'll see two voices shown on that -- or various voice numbers shown. Do you see those? And if you look down over to the next page, you'll see something that called "voice 6" and "voice 7." And then you'll find a place where it says, under voice 6, "Let's have that multiple rocket launcher, friend."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Top of our page 2, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you find it, can you let me know? You've found it, have you? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the passage I want you to follow with me is this. It starts there: "Let's have that multiple rocket launcher, friend. Get it ready for me, for Kacuni and Lugovi over there. Let me hear it roar." That voice is Kordic. The next voice is Blaskic: "When? Now?" Then Kordic: "It doesn't have to be right away. When we also ..." Next voice: "Well, you just tell me when." Next voice: "Listen, you prepare everything. Select the targets for the mortars and the VBR, and everything there is. Let's burn everything." Blaskic: "Well, I've already prepared that." Kordic: "You prepare everything and we're also preparing." Now, you were there. For what was your army preparing on or about the 24th of January, if it wasn't the attacks that were to follow on Merdani?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I really cannot confirm that this is an authentic conversation and who was involved in it. I do not have any information that something like that took place at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I want to ask you one other question about this transcript and I'll move on. From the account you've given to the Judges, at this time, you, the Croats, and in particular the Croats in Busovaca, had just suffered an attack by the Muslims. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January 1993. Your evidence is that there was an attack by the Muslims on the Croats in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that must have been uppermost in people's minds; correct? It must have been.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: But of course people had it on their minds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So if we read on from where you were, Blaskic says: You're preparing?" "Yes. Listen, stay there. We shall be in touch." Blaskic: "I'm here all the time. No problem." And then a reference to Botanic getting a Nora howitzer and a VBR ready for Zenica from Kordic. Blaskic: "That's good. Let him load 40 in the VBR and fire a salvo." Kordic: "I told him, I told him. But he won't do anything without an order. I told him we would strike if Zenica reacts. Otherwise, we won't. Just Kacuni." Was that a plan of which you were aware?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I did not know that plan, I do not know any details, and I simply can't believe that things were really happening as you are telling me they have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, read on. Blaskic saying: "They've asked for me over the TV." "Hmm?" Blaskic: "So shall I get in touch with them or not?" "What, over the TV?" "Well, it was announced over the TV that they've asked for me." "Forget that. Say you died. Say your funeral has been scheduled, friend, when we finish the job." "Okay." Then this, and please follow this: "They killed two of our boys, friend." That's from Kordic. "Two?" "Two of our boys killed in --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice, I think we have a problem with the interpretation, so will you please bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not following this, Mr. Prskalo, with what was being said?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I wasn't following the text, but I am listening to you attentively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll go more slowly, because there comes a time when Kordic says: "They killed two of our boys, friend." "Two?" "Two of our boys, they killed them perfidiously from behind at the checkpoint in Kacuni." Now, you remember the killing of those two people at Kacuni, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, at that time there were incidents in different places. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then it goes on, four lines further on, with Kordic saying: "One hundred should be killed for every one, friend," and he's going on over our page to say: "Squeeze them, and keep an eye on those in Fojnica, Kakanj and Visoko." It makes no reference, you see, this telephone conversation, to an attack on Busovaca, and it picks up the one provable event that had happened; namely, the loss of two men at Kacuni. That tape-recorder is telling the truth, isn't it? Namely, that at the time that you're saying there was an attack on Busovaca, there had been no such thing, and far from you being the victims, the HVO was in an aggressive mood; that's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot agree with that, because if that is so, then when is the crimes committed in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca at the time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not denying there were other bad things done by the Muslims in other places. But as to the attack on Busovaca, I'm challenging you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: The crimes that I'm referring to were a part of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Those exhibits can go back. Thank you. Exhibit 422.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Prskalo, you're claiming ignorance of lots of things, but in fact, as we see, your position was sometimes quite senior. Let's have a look at this next exhibit. It's 419.3, and it's coming your way. This is your handwriting, Mr. Prskalo; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Yes, this is evidently my document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is dated the 30th of January. On that day, you were present at peacekeeping or peacemaking negotiations. Maybe you wrote this letter there. But we can see that what you're saying is to a commander of the Ban Jelacic Brigade: "It would be useful if you would talk to Colonel Blaskic and appoint a member from Kiseljak to the Joint Commission. We signed a peace agreement. Send me a nomination as soon as possible. This member should be" -- something -- "at 9.00." Did you have the power to give instructions to commanders of brigades, please?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: To begin with, I must say that I did not have any commanding role. And this morning in my statement, I said that I absolutely did not play the role of a political commissar. This is merely a letter which has to do with the replenishment of the peace commission which was about to start its work. As you can see for yourself, this is an ordinary letter. It is no order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's a reverse to that letter, I believe. I'm not going to take time to go through it. It appears to be in someone else's hands. I'll make it available to the Defence. While I'm on that topic, the document from which I was effectively drawing this morning in dealing with the roles of the propaganda department is a document that's available to me, but at short notice. It isn't translated, and again I'll make that available to the Defence if they want to see it afterwards. It's only in B/C/S at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 3rd of February, we've heard evidence that the man called Jennings met Kordic, and it would appear from a document that he met him in your presence. Do you remember a British officer called Jennings, quite a young man, meeting Kordic? His evidence is that there were other men in the room, it would appear that you were one of them, and that you all sat very quietly while Kordic spoke for quite a long time, half an hour to 40 minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Could you tell me, where was that, what office? Is there anything more specific?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it was in the Hotel Vitez, unless I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I have no recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because what he's told us is that he asked Kordic whether he wanted to be "Colonel" or "Mister", and he accepted either, effectively. Would that be right? He was happy to be addressed as "Colonel", wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I cannot remember hearing anything like that. But when you are giving these facts to me, I should like to know whether that gentleman, that British citizen, was a member of the European Monitoring Mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake. It was the PTT building in Busovaca, and it was a British Battalion officer.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, then I believe if that was a part of our mission, Monitoring Mission in Busovaca, I remember that on one occasion, at the request -- because I wasn't the one who decided this, it was the European Monitors who decided where we would go and when, and I know that once they asked to go and see Mr. Dario Kordic because they wanted to discuss certain problems with him. Perhaps this could be that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to move as swiftly as I can with one other video that has to go into evidence. Your Honour, it's a long video. I'm going to ask the booth to play the first very short clip of the video which shows this witness, simply to identify it for him. And then I'm going to ask them to put in the other video, which is an extract from further on, which has Mr. Kordic. So that what you have in the transcripts coming your way are a transcript of all, the excerpt -- well, we'll ask the video booth to play the first video, and just for the purposes of identifying it for the witness, so that he can be satisfied with what it is. 652, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is it already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, this one is not in evidence, which is why I'm putting it into evidence now. Otherwise, I would deal with it even more briefly. I've only got a couple more exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Colonel Dario Kordic issued a public announcement and distributed it to all media and stated: Today the unity of the Croatian people is needed more than ever and the programme of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina has managed to unite all Croats, and now from the votive darkness which has surrounded us for 50 years, the so-called saviours of Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina have begun to emerge. These missions of the fascist-communist Yugoslav system are well known to all Croats wherever they are, and it is perfectly clear where this ship is heading. Croats do not need Yugoslavia anymore or a Bosnia and Herzegovina made to suit only one people. We want to build Bosnia-Herzegovina to suit all three constitutive peoples. We say to the founders of the Croat Peasants' Party in besieged Sarajevo and its leaders, Ivan Komso, Branko Mikulic and Stjepan Kljujic, that they had their historic chance to protect the Croatian people had they wanted to. Isn't this yet another desperate attempt by the order-givers to buy off a few professional and already-proven Croats who would then purport to represent Croatian interests in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as was done with the Croatian Party of Rights? It is sad that attempts are made to manipulate the reputation of the Croatian Peasants' Party, which the HDZ respects. We cannot help recalling those words from the Bible: "Beware of those in sheep's clothing who are ravenous wolves inside. By their deeds, you shall know them." At the very beginning, the public announcement will be read on behalf of the Operative Zone by Mr. Marko Prskalo, assistant commander for IPD. Please. Prskalo: After the tragic events in the territory of Busovaca, Muslim extremists, imbued with hatred for anything Croatian, are going even further."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Bennouna, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think they have the text, but not in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But even in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think they have it in English. No, there's a wave. Perhaps if we could take one more around. I'm sorry about that. While the next tape is being put in, which is 652A, which starts at the English translation page 18 and is marked, I'll just ask the witness this:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with the comment about Stjepan Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: Well, I can't say, because this release or this announcement was made by Madam Marija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Neither then nor at any other time did you disassociate yourself from the action taken to Mr. Kljujic, did you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRSKALO
utterances.text: I do not really know what was done to Mr. Kljujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honour, by the time you reach the side-lined page on page 18, Mr. Kordic had read out -- and that's why I'm not going to go through it -- the document signed by Boban and not signed by Izetbegovic. 595 is the exhibit number for that document. There's no need to take our time with that. But if we could now play 652A, it picks it up on page 18, and I intend to go through until the top of page 20.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] The free passage of people and goods shall be immediately established on all roads in the three regions of the said provinces. The HVO of the HZ HB expresses hope that Mr. Izetbegovic will realise the exceptional importance of this statement and sign it, since it also contains the wish for a much-wanted peace. At its session, the HVO of the HZ HB assumed the -- decided that if the above-mentioned statement is not signed by the leaders of the Muslim delegation, the basic assumptions of the peace plan concerning this issue shall be applied in the provinces, regardless of the separate agreement between the Croats and Muslims, which reads: according to which any national armed force must withdraw to its domicile provinces. If the joint statement is not implemented, the competent military and other bodies of the HZ HB HVO shall implement this paragraph of the basic document of the peace plan in the territory of the Provinces 3, 8 and 10. At the same time, the HVO of the HZ HB shall respect the competent government organs in the provinces where the other two nations dominate. The organisation of the police at the provisional level shall also be consistent with these principles. The police organs of the former MUP in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which shall cease to exist in Provinces 3, 8 and 10 within the framework of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna as soon as the already-signed documents of the Vance-Owen Plan enter into force, shall be informed with the public about the transfer of all competencies to the HZ HB Department of Internal Affairs in Province 3, 8 and 10. With regard to this, something has already been done. We have seen that new uniforms have arrived for members of the MUP, and these lads will thus have the task of maintaining peace and order in this region. Since the basic document and agreement on transitional organisation, the competencies of the future central government and the government in the HVO HZ HB provinces are clearly, any attempt to install different organs appointed by the present one-sided presidency and government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, such as districts, for instance, shall be prevented, whereas all decisions of the future transitional presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the transitional central government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be respected and implemented in the territories of Provinces 3, 8 and 10 in accordance with the obligations accepted with the signing of the peace plan.
